stages.stage: Stage 1 - Strategic Intake and Opportunity Definition
stages.approver: Sponsor for Class C, ratified in batch at the monthly Project Authority review; Project Authority for Class A and Class B
stages.exit: The need is real enough to investigate, an idea owner is identified, the work supports institutional or client value, and feasibility effort is justified.
items: Project idea / intake record: problem or opportunity, proposed outcome, beneficiaries, owner, urgency and known constraints
Current situation described with evidence that a problem or opportunity exists
Affected users, clients, services and institutional goals identified
Expected outcome stated without assuming a solution too early
Initial screening for legal, ethical, security, privacy, safety, financial and reputational concerns
Urgency, rough scale and project-versus-operations judgement recorded
Comparison against active commitments and resource capacity
Initial classification proposed (Class A / B / C) with reasons
Portfolio recommendation: proceed to feasibility, defer, merge, return or decline
Gate 1 decision recorded with approver, date and conditions
Expedited Gate 1/2 path used? If yes, record urgency justification, authority, maximum spend, time limit and stop authority (Section 4.6)

stages.decision: Approve the project charter and sponsor
stages.approver: Sponsor for Class B/C; Project Authority for Class A
stages.exit: A sponsor accepts accountability; the business case is credible; scope and intended outcome are clear; major risks are understood; suitable resources are likely available; and feasibility evidence supports proceeding.
items: Project charter completed against the Appendix B template
Proportionate business case prepared
Feasibility assessed: strategic, technical, operational, economic, schedule, legal/contractual, ethical/social and resource dimensions
Alternative approaches identified, including do nothing, buy, build, partner or change the process
High-level scope, exclusions, assumptions and acceptance concept prepared
Cost, duration, resource demand and expected benefits estimated as ranges where uncertainty is high
Principal risks, dependencies and constraints identified
Sponsor, project manager and key decision makers nominated
Software framework alignment recorded in the charter (software class, aligned G0-G6 checkpoints, Appendix I mapping)
Governance and tolerances recorded: decision rights, reporting, escalation, role separation, financial band, change authority
Benefits ownership, measures, default Gate 7 date and protected review effort recorded
Gate 2 decision recorded with approver, date and conditions

stages.stage: Stage 3 - Detailed Planning and Baseline Approval
stages.approver: Sponsor for Class B/C; Project Authority for Class A
stages.exit: The integrated plan is realistic; funds and people are committed; key requirements and acceptance criteria are testable; material risks have responses; controls and reporting are ready; and the sponsor formally authorises execution.
items: Scope statement, deliverables, exclusions, requirements and acceptance criteria
Work breakdown structure with manageable work packages
Schedule with dependencies, milestones, estimates, critical constraints and contingency
Budget, procurement, staff effort, tools, infrastructure and reserves
Responsibility assignment and decision authority (Appendix H, one accountable per activity)
Quality plan, review points, test strategy and evidence required for acceptance
Risk register, response actions, issue process and escalation thresholds
Communication, stakeholder engagement and reporting calendar
Security, privacy, data, access, backup, continuity and release controls where relevant
Change, configuration, version, document and records management method
Transition, training, support, handover, rollback and closure approach
Funded benefits-review effort, operational benefit owner and default Gate 7 due date
Baseline quality tests passed: complete, consistent, achievable, controlled, acceptable
Role separation meets Section 3.3, or compensating assurance approved and recorded
Plan readiness checklist (Appendix C) signed by Sponsor, PM and reviewers
Gate 3 decision recorded with approver, date and conditions

stages.decision: Accept work packages and authorise release or transition
stages.approver: Named acceptance authority; Project Authority concurrence for Class A
stages.exit: The deliverable meets agreed requirements; tests and reviews are evidenced; unresolved defects and risks are within approved limits; operations and users are ready; security and privacy conditions are satisfied; and release or transition authority is granted.
items: Formal kickoff held confirming objectives, roles, ways of working, reporting and escalation
Work packages authorised with outputs, owners, dates, quality criteria and dependencies
One controlled source maintained for plans, decisions, risks, issues, changes and deliverable versions
Deliverables reviewed early and progressively rather than at final testing only
Vendors, external contributors and client dependencies controlled against agreed obligations
Users, operations, training, support, data migration and release environments prepared in parallel
Work package acceptance evidence: output exists, checks passed, defects resolved or formally accepted, documentation updated, reviewer accepted
Test and review evidence identifying deliverable version and test environment
Defect and risk position within approved limits
Operational and user readiness confirmed
Security and privacy conditions satisfied
Gate 4 decision recorded with acceptance authority, date and conditions

stages.stage: Stage 5 - Continuous Monitoring, Control and Corrective Action (recurring from Gate 3 to Gate 6)
stages.decision: Continue, correct, rebaseline, escalate or stop
stages.approver: Sponsor within tolerance; Project Authority beyond tolerance or for Class A
stages.exit: Forecast performance remains acceptable, or a credible recovery/rebaseline decision has been approved. If value has disappeared, risk is unacceptable or recovery is not credible, the project must be paused, redirected or terminated.
items: Status reporting running at the class cadence (Class A weekly review plus formal status fortnightly; Class B monthly with fortnightly team review; Class C monthly plus midpoint check beyond 20 business days)
Minimum status report content complete: overall status, achievements, next period, schedule, cost/resources, scope/quality, risks/issues, decisions required
Status colour supported by evidence, not by activity or an unexpired deadline
Tolerance position measured against approved cost, schedule, scope, quality and risk limits
Variance analysis with root causes, consequences and corrective options

Gate 5 trigger log maintained (escalation trigger, forecast tolerance breach, material change, rebaseline, funding release, supplier failure, recovery plan, critical dependency change, doubtful acceptance, or a call by Sponsor/Authority/assurance)
Gate 5 convened within 2 business days for a red condition and 5 business days for any other material trigger
Corrective actions implemented, affected plans updated and effectiveness verified
Rebaseline decisions retain original commitment, approved changes and current forecast
Gate 5 decision recorded with approver, date and conditions

stages.exit: The authorised client or sponsor has accepted the outcome; operations own it; outstanding actions are assigned; finances and contracts are reconciled; records are archived; and the sponsor approves project closure.
items: Formal acceptance obtained against approved criteria, with accepted limitations recorded
Release, migration, training, support, security, backup, recovery and operational-readiness actions complete
Ownership transferred: products, data, licences, environments, documentation and unresolved actions
Contracts, invoices, assets, accounts and access rights closed or handed over
Budget reconciled; final cost, schedule, scope and quality performance recorded
Current versions, approvals, evidence, decisions, lessons and closure records archived
People and resources released responsibly and contributions acknowledged
Benefits measures, owners, review dates and outstanding corrective actions assigned
Records reviewed against the Appendix J retention schedule; legal holds identified
Project register status set to 'Operational - Benefits Pending' with Gate 7 due date and evidence owner
Closure report completed (Appendix G)
Gate 6 decision recorded with approver, date and conditions

stages.stage: Stage 7 - Benefits Realisation and Post-Project Review
stages.decision: Confirm benefits, corrective actions and lessons
stages.approver: Project Sponsor, supported by the Service / Operations Owner
stages.exit: Benefits evidence is reviewed, remaining actions have owners, important lessons are incorporated into institutional practice and leadership decides whether to sustain, improve, expand, replace or retire the outcome.
items: Benefits plan complete: benefit, baseline, measure, target, owner, dependencies and review dates
Protected review effort used as budgeted at Gate 3 (Class A two person-days, Class B one, Class C half)
Usage evidence gathered: is the product or capability being used as intended?
Outcome evidence gathered: service, revenue, efficiency, learning, quality, safety or client improvement
Costs, delays, negative impacts or risks transferred elsewhere identified
Correct and incorrect assumptions reviewed
Corrective actions, follow-on investment or retirement decisions identified with owners
Lessons routed into institutional standards or training content
Project register status changed to 'Closed - Benefits Reviewed'
Gate 7 decision recorded with approver, date and conditions

tracks.name: Software Development and Engineering Track
tracks.source: Software Development and Engineering Framework v1.2

stages.decision: Authorise discovery or decline the request
stages.exit: The problem and intended benefits are clear enough to investigate; ownership and discovery resources are assigned; material legal, privacy, security or procurement blockers are identified; and management has approved, deferred or declined in writing.
items: Project request or concept note
Preliminary business case and feasibility assessment (technical, economic, operational, schedule, legal, data, security, resource)
Named sponsor, delivery lead and technical owner
Initial scope, stakeholder list, risk class and risk register
Alternatives considered, including process change, configuration or acquisition instead of custom development
Discovery effort estimated and authority to proceed obtained
G0 decision record
No coding started as an informal commitment before owner, outcome, data constraints and acceptance authority exist

stages.exit: Each committed requirement is necessary, clear, feasible, testable, traceable and prioritised; conflicts and ambiguities are resolved or assigned with dates and owners; the acceptance authority approves the baseline; and scope, schedule and cost assumptions align with the approved requirements.
items: Software Requirements Specification, product backlog or equivalent controlled requirements set
Functional requirements, business rules, data needs, interfaces, roles and permissions documented

Non-functional requirements defined: security, privacy, performance, availability, reliability, accessibility, usability, compatibility, maintainability, scalability, portability, logging, backup and recovery
User journeys, process maps, use cases or stories as appropriate
Acceptance criteria and initial test conditions
Data inventory and classification (Public / Internal / Confidential / Restricted)
Preliminary privacy and security requirements
Requirements traceability matrix or linked work-item structure
Requirements reviewed with affected stakeholders and formally baselined
Requirement quality rules applied: clear, atomic, feasible, testable, traceable, consistent, controlled
Unresolved-question log with owners and dates
G1 approval recorded

stages.stage: Stage 3 - Planning, architecture and detailed design
stages.approver: Technical lead; security reviewer for higher risk
stages.exit: The design addresses the approved functional and non-functional requirements; interfaces, data ownership, trust boundaries and failure modes are understood; critical risks are reduced, accepted or assigned to a dated action; and build, test, deployment and operational approaches are feasible and funded.
items: Project delivery plan and updated estimates
Assurance effort, schedule and budget as a distinct line item; commercial disclosure for Class 3 and Class 4 client work
Architecture description with context, component, deployment and data-flow views
Architecture Decision Records for material choices, including rejected alternatives
UX prototypes/designs, database model and API/interface specifications
Threat model and privacy assessment
Security design: authentication, authorisation, secrets, encryption, logging and recovery controls
Test strategy, environment plan, migration approach, observability, support model, backup and rollback concept
Risky assumptions validated with controlled prototypes or spikes
Architecture expectations addressed: modularity, least privilege, failure containment, observability, recoverability, technology fitness
G2 review and approval record

stages.exit: All committed work is merged through the approved review path; the build is reproducible and automated checks pass or have approved exceptions; no unresolved critical defect, exposed secret or prohibited component is known; and the test environment holds an identifiable release candidate.
items: Version-controlled source code, configuration and infrastructure definitions
Work items, commits and pull/merge requests linked with reviewer evidence
Protected release branches enforced; merges require successful checks and review
Peer review completed (two-person or specialist review for critical security, data, payment or infrastructure changes)
Unit tests written with the code; integration, contract or component tests added where interfaces are affected
Continuous integration passing: formatting, linting, build, test, secret and dependency/security scans
Successful automated build and test results retained
Dependency and licence inventory; software bill of materials where required
Secrets held in an approved secret store and absent from code, fixtures, logs and collaboration tools
AI- or tool-generated code reviewed, tested and accepted by a competent human
Architecture, API, data, operational and user documentation updated with the change
Known-defect, technical-debt and deviation records
G3 code-complete decision

stages.stage: Stage 5 - Verification, validation and acceptance / Stage 6 - Release and deployment
stages.approver: Product owner, service owner and release authority (Executive Sponsor or delegate for Class 3-4; Technical Lead for Class 1-2); QA lead confirms verification evidence, independent QA for Class 3, independent or specialist QA for Class 4
stages.exit: Every release requirement has passed evidence or an explicitly accepted deviation; no open Severity 1 or unaccepted Severity 2 defect remains; security, privacy and operational risks meet the release criteria; the release candidate and evidence set are uniquely identified and protected from uncontrolled change; release approval is recorded before production change except under the emergency-change process; deployment completed successfully or rollback restored the approved service state; monitoring shows acceptable service health; and support and service owners accept the deployed version and known issues.
items: Approved risk-based test plan with traceability to requirements
Test cases, automated suites, actual results and evidence recorded with environment, build identifier and tester
Unit, integration, contract, system, regression and user-acceptance tests executed as applicable
Security, privacy, performance, accessibility, compatibility, migration, backup/restore and resilience testing according to risk
Production-like environments used with representative, lawful test data and no uncontrolled production-data copying
Defect register with severity, disposition, owner and retest status
Corrections retested and targeted regression tests run
No open S1 defect; any S2 released only with documented residual-risk acceptance
Security/privacy scan and review records
User-acceptance record from the authorised product owner or client representative
Release package assembled: version, approved changes, dependencies, configuration, migration and known limitations
Release notes and immutable release/build identifier
Production access, infrastructure, capacity, monitoring, backup, support and communication readiness confirmed
Approved deployment, data migration, rollback and communication plans with named decision authority
Build and deployment credentials kept separate; deployment automated and repeatable where practical
Affected data backed up or checkpointed; restoration or rollback feasibility validated before irreversible change
Operational runbook, monitoring/alert configuration and support handover ready
Release-readiness checklist (Appendix F) completed across scope, requirements, code, tests, security/privacy, dependencies, data, operations, deployment and approval
Release authority is not the sole author of the release (role separation for Class 3-4)
Deployment executed with smoke tests and business verification; actual deployment, deviations, approvers and outcome recorded
G4 release readiness decision recorded

stages.decision: Confirm stable service and close transition
stages.exit: The service remains within approved operational and security limits; incidents, vulnerabilities and maintenance obligations have accountable owners and target dates; access, dependencies, data retention and continuity controls are reviewed periodically; and management receives sufficient evidence to continue, improve, replace or retire the service.
items: Service catalogue entry, named service owner and support model
Deployment record, smoke tests and early-life review
Monitoring of availability, performance, capacity, errors, security events, backups, certificate expiry and critical dependencies
Documented support channels, service hours, escalation paths and response targets
Incident, problem, change, maintenance and vulnerability records
Root-cause analysis for significant or recurring incidents with tracked corrective actions
Vulnerability remediation within service targets (critical: 7 days Class 3-4, 14 days Class 2; high: 30 days Class 3-4, 60 days Class 2)
S1 incident acknowledgement within target (1 hour Class 3-4, 4 hours Class 2)
Backup restoration tested on schedule (quarterly Class 3-4, at least semi-annually Class 2) with results compared to RPO/RTO
Access review completed on schedule (quarterly Class 3-4, at least annually Class 2)
Enhancements and changes processed through the same traceability, review, testing and release controls
Service review reports and improvement backlog maintained
G5 operational acceptance recorded

stages.approver: Sponsor, data owner and service owner
stages.exit: Users and stakeholders have been notified and supported through transition; required data is preserved or transferred and unneeded data securely disposed of; no orphaned credential, public endpoint, paid service or unmanaged dependency remains; and the sponsor, data owner and service owner approve closure.
items: Retirement reason, affected users, replacement service, dependencies and approved date confirmed
Transition and communication plan, including data export or migration
Retention, archival, transfer or secure-deletion decisions applied to data and records
Accounts, credentials, integrations, domains, certificates, pipelines, infrastructure and supplier services disabled
Source, releases, configuration, decisions, test evidence, licences and operational records archived
Final asset inventory and archive location recorded
Financial and contractual closure verified
Lessons learned, benefits achieved and outstanding actions captured
Client or sponsor acceptance recorded
G6 closure decision

artefact_floor.floor: C1: purpose, owner, scope, risk class and disposal date. C2-4: request/charter, feasibility, stakeholders, scope and risk.
C1: acceptance note; full requirements when user-facing, integrated or persistent data is used. C2-4: requirements/backlog, acceptance, data classification and traceability.
C1: design note for material interface, data or security risk. C2: architecture and test/deployment design. C3-4: add threat/privacy and specialist assurance.
Controlled source/configuration, review evidence, build/CI results and component inventory. C1 may use simplified review evidence but must retain source control and basic testing.
C1: basic acceptance and defect record. C2-4: plan, cases, results, defects, security/privacy and user acceptance at class depth.
C1: demonstration/non-production release record only; any production use requires reclassification. C2-4: release notes, approval, migration, deployment, rollback and validation.
C2-4: runbooks, monitoring, access, backup/recovery, support, incidents, targets and reviews. A Class 1 experiment must be reclassified before operational reliance.
C1: disposal date, access removal and data/code disposition. C2-4: acceptance/closure, data disposition, decommissioning, archive and lessons.

alignment.rule: Use one intake record, sponsor, feasibility screen and initial classification decision.
Combine when requirements and acceptance criteria are sufficiently mature. If G1 follows later, reuse the charter and add only the requirements evidence; do not repeat the business decision.
Use one integrated readiness pack covering project baseline, architecture, security/privacy, test, deployment, assurance and operational plans.

alignment.sdlc: G3 prerequisite and G4 - Release Readiness
alignment.rule: G3 code-complete evidence is an engineering prerequisite. One G4/Gate 4 approval pack authorises release under the stricter approver set.

alignment.sdlc: G3 or G5 evidence where relevant
alignment.rule: Gate 5 is recurring or triggered project governance. Engineering or early-life evidence may support it; no duplicate gate is required solely because numbering differs.

alignment.sdlc: G5 - Operational Acceptance and G6 - Retirement/Closure
alignment.rule: Use G5 evidence for handover. Use G6 when the project closes or a service is retired. One closure record may satisfy both where scope matches.

alignment.sdlc: Post-implementation review evidence; no separate software gate
alignment.rule: Use service measures and the software review as evidence for the single Gate 7 benefits decision.

class_mapping.interpretation: Class 1 is permitted only for time-bound, non-production experimentation with no real personal, client-confidential or payment data. Any operational or production use is at least Class 2.
Use Class 3 where personal/sensitive data, public exposure, finance/identity, material reputation, contractual service levels or significant recovery impact exists.
Use Class 4 for safety-significant, critical-infrastructure, large-scale restricted-data or mission-critical services. Executive governance and explicit residual-risk acceptance apply.

measures.measure: Milestone reliability = milestones achieved on or before the approved date / milestones due
measures.source_owner: Approved schedule and status reports / Project Manager; consolidated by Framework Owner

measures.measure: Absolute cost forecast variance = |forecast total cost - approved budget| / approved budget
measures.source_owner: Budget, commitments and forecast / Project Manager and Finance
measures.target: Within class tolerance: A 5%, B 10%, C 15%

measures.measure: First-pass acceptance rate = deliverables accepted without material rework / deliverables presented
measures.source_owner: Acceptance and defect records / Quality Reviewer or acceptance authority
measures.frequency: At each acceptance event; quarterly portfolio total

measures.measure: Overdue critical risk actions = count of critical-risk actions past their approved due date
measures.source_owner: Risk register / Project Manager; challenged by Assurance
measures.frequency: Weekly on project; monthly portfolio total

measures.measure: On-time Gate 7 completion = Gate 7 decisions completed by due date / Gate 7 reviews due
measures.source_owner: Project register and benefits records / Framework Owner and Sponsor

measures.measure: Delivery flow: median lead time from authorised work item to accepted release, with material delay reasons
measures.target: Set by project; trend must not deteriorate

measures.measure: Defect escape rate = production defects / total defects found in testing and production, reported with severity
measures.target: Set by project; severity trend reported

measures.measure: Availability: observed production-service availability against the approved service target
Open vulnerability age by severity against institutional service targets
Gate compliance = applicable gates with required evidence and approval recorded before the governed commitment

example: Because the bank API sandbox has no certification slot before November, there is a possibility that connectivity testing slips, resulting in a Gate 4 delay
Book a certification slot and prepare an aggregator fallback path
risk.note: Use the form: Because of [cause], there is a possibility that [uncertain event], resulting in [effect on objectives]. For issues, state what has happened, current impact, immediate containment, root-cause owner and resolution date.

columns: Quality, security, privacy and operational impact
example: Add multi-currency display conversion to the first release
+5 business days on the build milestone
Adds an exchange-rate dependency requiring availability monitoring
Improves client acceptance likelihood; adds a third-party dependency risk
Reject / defer / substitute / reduce other scope / approve
change.note: A change becomes part of the project only after need, impact, alternatives, risks, cost, schedule, quality and benefits are assessed and the correct authority approves it.

columns: Exact requirement that cannot be met
example: Independent QA for a Class 3 release (Appendix A testing floor)
No second qualified tester available in the delivery window
Bank connectivity module; no personal data in test
Moderate residual risk of undetected regression
External reviewer appointed for regression evidence; extended smoke test set
Reviewer report and test results attached
Recruit or contract a QA reviewer before the next release - Delivery Lead
exception.note: Types: Exception (approved, time-bound deviation) or Non-conformance (required process or evidence absent, inaccurate or bypassed). An expired exception is non-compliance. An exception may never authorise unlawful conduct. Critical non-conformance blocks the relevant gate.

columns: Reason (contain / restore / prevent harm / urgent security)
example: Payments read API pod restart and config rollback
Full regression pack; final release notes
emergency.note: Software, production-service or client-data emergencies follow the SDLC emergency-change procedure: named authority and deputy, non-waivable minimum record, deferrable-evidence list and a retrospective review within 72 hours of stabilisation. All other projects: Sponsor records the same elements and convenes a review within 5 business days.

example: Integrated plan, architecture, threat model, test strategy, benefits funding
Confirm the QA reviewer before the first build increment
decision.note: Gate decisions are one of: Approve, Approve with conditions, Hold, Redirect, Terminate. Unresolved critical conditions cannot be treated as 'approve with conditions'.
